author: globeandmail
title: Alanis Morissette mixes melancholia with mistletoe in first-ever holiday album
text: Alanis Morissette mixes melancholia with mistletoe in first-ever holiday album Good Weather for Immaculate Conception has carols, covers and two new original songs On her debut holiday album of carols, covers and a pair of new originals, Alanis Morissette sings that all is calm and all is bright, and a “rum-pa-pum pum” to all. Tis the season, right? Not for everybody. The weather outside is frightful, and sometimes things aren’t so great inside either. Which is why on the tastefully done and playfully titled LP Good Weather for Immaculate Conception Morissette mixes melancholia with mistletoe.For the less than festive, the societal expectation to be jolly during the holiday season is just more stress. Alanis feels you, literally.“You don’t have to smile for us, nor have a joyous time,” she assures on To an Empath at Christmas Time , one of the album’s new original songs. “You don’t have to hold your breath until New Year’s time. ” The Ottawa-born Jagged Little Pill superstar has addressed this intimate compassion before.This is her on 2012’s Empathy : “Thank you for seeing me, I feel so less lonely\/ Thank you for getting me …\" There’s always been a degree of cynicism attached to holiday albums. Artists release them for a variety of reasons: nostalgia and genuine Christmas cheer, sure, but also because the records don’t require newly written material. It’s also true that traditional songs come cheap because the copyrights are typically expired.Perhaps most importantly, holiday music is the gift that keeps on giving. All Mariah Carey wants for Christmas every year is for people to stream her seasonal classic from 1994. As well, touring artists with December-specific music are annually able to sell concert tickets. Isn’t it ironic that consumerism and spirituality exist together so agreeably?We can’t know Morissette’s motivations regarding Good Weather for Immaculate Conception , her first studio album since 2022’s The Storm Before the Calm . She’s been putting out holiday songs for years now: The previously released versions of O Holy Night , What Child is This? , Happy Xmas , Little Drummer Boy and Last Christmas are all gathered on the new album.Among the guest artists are actor\/banjoist Steve Martin and the serial collaborator Brandi Carlile, who contributed to the lead single Beautiful Star of Bethlehem . Comedic actor Martin Short makes what might seem to be a surprise appearance on Merry Christmas , but as a child he dreamed of being a crooner. Short acquits himself well here, doing it Sinatra’s way. Morissette brings nothing new to Joni Mitchell’s poignant River .The song is bullet-proof, though − I can’t imagine ever not wanting to hear it, any time of year. The album’s other new original is Christmas on the Dancefloor , which stomps around like an old Serena Ryder hit. Christmas means different things to different people, but this pounding track is lazy and contrived. The best holiday songs can be whatever the listener needs them to be, fitting their moods − wistful, joyous or jingled − as required.Otherwise, Good Weather for Immaculate Conception is evenly wrought and mostly minimalist, with production that alternates between acoustic and electro approaches. The best angels greet with anthems sweet, and Morissette understood the assignment.
